## CodemodeSandboxDurableObject  codemode/src/cloudflare.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * The remote end of `RemoteCodemodeSandbox`: a Durable Object whose one RPC method runs a script's
 * VM and calls back into the client for every tool call.
 *
 * Deploy it as its own Worker and bind it from the Worker that runs your agent with `script_name`.
 * A separate Worker is what keeps scripts off the agent's thread: a class in the same Worker can
 * share an isolate, and therefore a thread, with the objects that call it.
 *
 * The object keeps no state between executions and never touches storage. Executions that reach
 * the same instance share its thread: they interleave while they wait on tools, and a script that
 * computes delays the others. Name instances per session (`getByName(sessionId)`) to keep one
 * session's scripts together, or per execution for full independence.
 *
 * Limits apply to every request, whatever the client asks for. Override the fields in a subclass:
 *
 *     export class CodemodeSandbox extends CodemodeSandboxDurableObject {
 *       protected maxInterruptBudget = 200_000;
 *     }
 */
export class CodemodeSandboxDurableObject<Env = unknown> extends DurableObject<Env> {
	/** Called by `RemoteCodemodeSandbox` over RPC. Resolves when the script has settled or was stopped. */
	execute(request: CodemodeRemoteRequest, exchange: CodemodeRemoteExchange): Promise<void>
}

## resolveSchemaRef  codemode/src/declarations.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * The subschema a local `$ref` (`#`, `#/$defs/Item`) names in `root`, or undefined for remote references and
 * references that name nothing. Pointer segments are URI-decoded and JSON Pointer unescaped (`~1` is `/`, `~0` is `~`).
 */
export function resolveSchemaRef(ref: string, root: unknown): CodemodeJsonSchema | undefined

## schemaToType  codemode/src/declarations.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Convert a JSON Schema to a TypeScript type expression: objects on one line (`{ a: string; b?: number; }`) with properties sorted by name,
 * or one property per line with `//` comments when a property has a description or constraints the
 * type cannot express (`// @integer @minimum 1 @default 20`); `Array<T>` for arrays. Local references
 * (`#/$defs/...`, `#/definitions/...`) resolve against `schema`; recursive and remote references
 * render as `unknown`. A result longer than `maxChars` is rendered again without the constraint tags,
 * and renders as `unknown` if it is still too long.
 */
export function schemaToType(schema: CodemodeJsonSchema, options: { maxChars?: number } = {}): string

 * identifier become `_`. `mcp__docs__search` stays as is, `my-tool` becomes `my_tool`.

export function toCodemodeIdentifier(name: string): string

## CodemodeSandboxBase  codemode/src/runtime/execution.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/**
 * Tool table, defaults, and in-flight executions; the behavior every sandbox shares. Subclasses
 * only choose where the VM runs by passing a {@link VmLauncher}.
 *
 * The script sees `tools.<name>(args)` for every registered tool, `ALL_TOOLS`, the output helpers
 * `text`, `image`, `exit`, and `console.*`, `store`/`load`, and the configured globals; nothing
 * else (no timers, `fetch`, `process`, `require`, modules). Each `execute()` gets its own VM; the
 * sandbox only holds the tool table and defaults. `close()` aborts in-flight executions.
 */
export class CodemodeSandboxBase {
	constructor(options: CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions, launch: VmLauncher)
	/** Throws if a tool with the same name is already registered. */
	registerTool(tool: CodemodeTool): void
	unregisterTool(name: string): boolean
	get tools(): CodemodeTool[]
	get globals(): CodemodeTool[]
	/**
	 * `code` is an async function body: `return` and top-level `await` work.
	 * Never rejects for script failures; those come back as `{ ok: false }`.
	 * The script can use `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` on `options.store`.
	 */
	execute(code: string, options: CodemodeExecuteOptions = {}): Promise<CodemodeResult>
	/**
	 * Run `code` deterministically, with the caller answering its calls: the same script, start time, seed, tools,
	 * globals, and store, answered with the same results in the same `seq` order, makes the same calls with the same
	 * arguments and produces the same output, on any VM with the same fingerprint. A host can therefore replay it
	 * after a restart. The VM runs in UTC, its clock reads `startedAt` and then the `now` of the result being
	 * processed, its randomness comes from `seed`, and `WeakRef` and `FinalizationRegistry` do not exist.
	 *
	 * The sandbox's own tools and globals are not used: the run declares its own, and every call goes to
	 * `options.onCall`. Never rejects for script failures; abort through `options.signal` to end the run with an
	 * error the script cannot catch.
	 */
	start(code: string, options: CodemodeRunOptions): CodemodeRun
	/** Aborts in-flight executions (they resolve with `kind: "aborted"`) and rejects new ones. */
	async close(): Promise<void>
}

## VmChannel  codemode/src/runtime/execution.ts
used by: codemode-effect via CodemodeSandboxBase, durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** The host's handle on a running VM. */
export interface VmChannel {
	post(message: HostToWorkerMessage): void;
	/** Requests VM shutdown. Called once; may resolve before a worker or remote VM actually exits. */
	stop(): Promise<void>;
}

## VmEvents  codemode/src/runtime/execution.ts
used by: codemode-effect via CodemodeSandboxBase, durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** Callbacks a launcher uses to report what its VM does. */
export interface VmEvents {
	/** A message from the VM. Validated here, so launchers can pass through anything they receive. */
	message(message: unknown): void;
	/** The VM failed or stopped outside the bridge, for example a worker exit or a remote error. */
	failure(error: CodemodeError): void;
}

## VmLauncher  codemode/src/runtime/execution.ts
used by: codemode-effect via CodemodeSandboxBase, durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/**
 * Starts a VM for one execution. Rejections become `sandbox` errors with the rejection's message.
 * The VM may start reporting messages before the returned promise settles.
 */
export type VmLauncher = (data: VmStartData, events: VmEvents) => VmChannel | Promise<VmChannel>;

## CodemodeSandbox  codemode/src/runtime/host.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Runs JavaScript in a QuickJS VM (a separate wasm instance) inside a worker thread. The worker
 * keeps script execution off the host thread: QuickJS runs synchronously, so a spinning script on
 * the host thread would block its event loop. Requires `node:worker_threads` (Node or Bun); see
 * `InlineCodemodeSandbox` and `RemoteCodemodeSandbox` in `@earendil-works/pi-codemode/portable`
 * for other runtimes.
 */
export class CodemodeSandbox extends CodemodeSandboxBase {
	constructor(options: CodemodeSandboxOptions = {})
}

## DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_BUDGET  codemode/src/runtime/inline.ts
used by: codemode-effect
export const DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_BUDGET: 100000

## InlineCodemodeSandbox  codemode/src/runtime/inline.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Runs each execution's QuickJS VM on the calling thread. Works in any runtime with WebAssembly
 * and microtasks; needs no worker threads, files, or Node built-ins. A script that computes
 * blocks the caller's thread until it awaits a tool or uses up its interrupt budget, so prefer
 * `CodemodeSandbox` where worker threads exist, and `RemoteCodemodeSandbox` to keep scripts off a
 * thread that must stay responsive (such as a Durable Object that serves a session).
 */
export class InlineCodemodeSandbox extends CodemodeSandboxBase {
	constructor(options: InlineCodemodeSandboxOptions)
}

## InlineCodemodeSandboxOptions  codemode/src/runtime/inline.ts
used by: codemode-effect
export interface InlineCodemodeSandboxOptions extends CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions {
	/**
	 * Compiled `quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm`. On Cloudflare, import it with Wrangler's `CompiledWasm`
	 * rule (`@earendil-works/pi-codemode/cloudflare` does this); on Node, `loadQuickJSWasm()`.
	 */
	wasm: CodemodeWasmModule | Promise<CodemodeWasmModule>;
	/**
	 * Interrupt polls an execution may use before it fails with `kind: "timeout"`. The only limit on
	 * a script that computes without awaiting a tool. Default: {@link DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_BUDGET}.
	 */
	interruptBudget?: number;
}

## MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS  codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Output one script may produce with `text()`, `image()`, and `console.*`: characters of text and
 * base64 image data, and items. The host keeps all output until the script ends, so without a
 * limit a script that prints in a loop grows the host's memory until it crashes. The item limit
 * covers loops that print empty strings.
 */
export const MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS: number

## MAX_STORE_TOTAL_CHARS  codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts
used by: codemode-effect

## MAX_STORE_VALUE_CHARS  codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * JavaScript evaluated inside the QuickJS VM before the script runs.
 *
 * The VM is its own wasm instance, so nothing here guards a realm boundary.
 * The prelude keeps the host bridge in a closure so the script cannot call it
 * directly, and builds `tools`, `ALL_TOOLS`, the output helpers (`text`, `image`,
 * `exit`, `console`), and globals on top of it. Tool arguments and results cross
 * as JSON strings and are parsed on this side.
 *
 * Output helpers: `text(value)` appends a text item (non-strings are
 * JSON-stringified), `image(urlOrItem)` appends an image from a base64 `data:` URL, an
 * `{ image_url }` object, or an image block `{ type: "image", data, mimeType }`, and `exit()` ends the script
 * successfully. `console.*` appends text items marked as console output.
 *
 * `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` are synchronous: they work on a snapshot of
 * JSON text passed in as `storeJson`, and the keys the script wrote are reported
 * with a successful "done".
 *
 * Evaluates to a function `(bridge, toolsJson, globalsJson, storeJson) => { settle, run, stalled }`.
 * `settle(id, ok, payload, propertiesJson)` settles call `id`; a rejection's `Error` gets the own properties of the
 * `propertiesJson` object, except `name`, `message`, and `stack`.
 * `toolsJson` lists `{ name, jsName, description }`: `tools[jsName]` and `tools[name]` call the
 * tool, and `ALL_TOOLS` lists `{ name: jsName, description }`.
 * `stalled()` reports a script that has not finished while no host call is pending: with no timers
 * or I/O in the VM, nothing can ever resume it.
 * `globalsJson` lists `{ name, spread }`; `a.b` names are grouped into a frozen `a` object.
 * `bridge(kind, a, b, c)` with kind "call" or "global" (id, name, argsJson),
 * "output" ("text" or "console", text) or ("image", data, mimeType), or "done" (ok, valueJsonOrErrorJson, writesJson).
 *
 * Before anything else the prelude freezes the built-ins and makes the built-in globals read-only.
 * The prelude shares them with the script, so a script that patched one (for example
 * `Array.prototype.toJSON`) could otherwise corrupt what the prelude reports to the host.
 */
export const MAX_STORE_VALUE_CHARS: number

## HostToWorkerMessage  codemode/src/runtime/protocol.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export type HostToWorkerMessage =
	/**
	 * `payload` is the JSON result when `ok`, otherwise the error message. Deterministic mode: `seq` numbers the
	 * results from 1 in the order the VM applies them, and the VM's clock reads `now` while it processes this one.
	 */
	{
		type: "result";
		id: number;
		ok: boolean;
		payload: string | undefined;
		seq?: number;
		now?: number;
		/** Deterministic mode, `ok: false`: a JSON object whose properties the script's `Error` gets. */
		properties?: string;
	};

## ScriptErrorJson  codemode/src/runtime/protocol.ts
used by: codemode-effect via WorkerToHostMessage
/** JSON-encoded `{ name?, message, stack? }` of an error thrown by the script. */
export type ScriptErrorJson = string;

## VmStartData  codemode/src/runtime/protocol.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/**
 * Messages between the host (main thread) and the worker. Tool arguments,
 * results, and values cross as JSON strings: the worker passes them into and
 * out of the QuickJS VM as strings and never builds structured values itself.
 */

/**
 * Everything a VM needs to run one script, independent of where it runs. Plain data, so it can
 * cross a `postMessage` or a Workers RPC call unchanged.
 */
export interface VmStartData {
	code: string;
	/** `jsName` is the identifier the script uses; `description` is listed in `ALL_TOOLS`. */
	tools: { name: string; jsName: string; description: string }[];
	globals: { name: string; spread: boolean }[];
	memoryLimitBytes: number | undefined;
	/** Snapshot for `load()`: key to JSON text. */
	store: Record<string, string>;
	/**
	 * Run deterministically (`CodemodeSandboxBase.start()`): UTC, a virtual clock starting at `startedAt` (ms since
	 * the epoch) that moves only with delivered results, randomness from `seed`, no `WeakRef`, results applied in
	 * `seq` order, and `started`/`idle` messages.
	 */
	deterministic?: { startedAt: number; seed: number };
}

## WorkerToHostMessage  codemode/src/runtime/protocol.ts
used by: codemode-effect
export type WorkerToHostMessage =
	| { type: "call"; id: number; target: "tool" | "global"; name: string; args: string | undefined }
	| { type: "output"; item: CodemodeOutputItem }
	/**
	 * `writes` is a JSON array of `[key, json]` for `store()` and `[key]` for deletions. Deterministic mode: `during`
	 * is the result the VM was processing when the script finished (0: its first run) and the calls issued by then.
	 */
	| { type: "done"; ok: true; value: string | undefined; writes: string; during?: CodemodeDuring }
	| { type: "done"; ok: false; error: ScriptErrorJson; during?: CodemodeDuring }
	/** The VM failed outside the script's control, for example a wasm trap. */
	| { type: "crash"; message: string }
	/** Deterministic mode, before the script runs: what the VM is, so a replay can refuse a different one. */
	| { type: "started"; fingerprint: string }
	/**
	 * Deterministic mode, after the script waits again: having processed result `seq` (0: the script's first run), it
	 * has issued `issued` calls in total.
	 */
	| { type: "idle"; seq: number; issued: number };

## CodemodeRemoteReply  codemode/src/runtime/remote.ts
used by: codemode-effect

 * The client's answer to an exchange: the result of the call the exchange carried, `null` when it
 * carried no call, or `stop` once the client no longer wants the execution.
 */
export type CodemodeRemoteReply = HostToWorkerMessage | { type: "stop" } | null;

## RemoteCodemodeSandbox  codemode/src/runtime/remote.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Runs each execution's VM on a remote, usually a Cloudflare Durable Object deployed with
 * `CodemodeSandboxDurableObject`, while tools run here. Same API and results as
 * `CodemodeSandbox`, so it can replace it. Differences: a script that computes without calling a
 * tool is limited by the remote's interrupt budget rather than `timeoutMs`, and after a deadline or
 * abort the remote VM keeps computing until it next calls a tool or uses up that budget.
 */
export class RemoteCodemodeSandbox extends CodemodeSandboxBase {
	constructor(options: RemoteCodemodeSandboxOptions)
}

## RemoteCodemodeSandboxOptions  codemode/src/runtime/remote.ts
used by: codemode-effect
export interface RemoteCodemodeSandboxOptions extends CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions {
	/**
	 * Returns the remote that runs one execution, called once per `execute()`. For a Durable Object,
	 * pick the instance here, for example `() => env.CODEMODE_SANDBOX.getByName(sessionId)`.
	 */
	remote: () => CodemodeRemote;
	/** Interrupt budget requested from the remote. Default: the remote's default. */
	interruptBudget?: number;
}

## serveCodemodeRemote  codemode/src/runtime/remote.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Remote side of {@link RemoteCodemodeSandbox}: runs one execution's VM on this thread and
 * forwards everything it reports through `exchange`. Resolves once the VM has stopped and the
 * terminal message has been delivered, or the client asked to stop. Never rejects.
 */
export function serveCodemodeRemote(
	request: CodemodeRemoteRequest,
	exchange: CodemodeRemoteExchange,
	options: CodemodeServeOptions,
): Promise<void>

	name: string;
	/**
	 * The identifier the script uses, `tools.<jsName>`. Default: `toCodemodeIdentifier(name)`. A host that replays a run

	issued: number;

## CodemodeError  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export interface CodemodeError {
	kind: CodemodeErrorKind;
	name?: string;
	message: string;
	stack?: string;
}

## CodemodeErrorKind  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export type CodemodeErrorKind =
	/** The script threw or failed to parse. `name` and `stack` come from the script's error. */
	| "script"
	/**
	 * The overall deadline expired, or a VM on the calling thread used up its interrupt budget.
	 * The execution ended and the VM was asked to stop; a worker or remote VM may still be computing.
	 */
	| "timeout"
	/** The caller's signal fired or the sandbox was closed. The execution ended and the VM was asked to stop. */
	| "aborted"
	/**
	 * The VM or its transport failed outside the script's control (for example a wasm trap, a missing
	 * worker file, or a remote sandbox that failed).
	 */
	| "sandbox";

## CodemodeExecuteOptions  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export interface CodemodeExecuteOptions {
	signal?: AbortSignal;
	/** Overrides the sandbox default for this execution. */
	timeoutMs?: number;
	/**
	 * Values the script reads with `load(key)`. Must be JSON-serializable. The script's own
	 * `store()` calls come back as `result.storeWrites`; persisting them is up to the caller.
	 */
	store?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}

## CodemodeHostCall  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** A call the script made in a {@link CodemodeSandboxBase.start} run, answered with `CodemodeRun.deliver()`. */
export interface CodemodeHostCall {
	/** The VM's own number for the call, `1`, `2`, ... in the order the script made its calls (tools and globals). */
	id: number;
	target: "tool" | "global";
	name: string;
	/** What the script passed, after a JSON round trip; for spread globals the argument list. */
	args: unknown;
}

## CodemodeJsonSchema  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** A JSON Schema document. Only used to render declarations; values are not validated against it. */
export type CodemodeJsonSchema = { [key: string]: unknown } | boolean;

## CodemodeOutcome  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/**
 * A call's answer. A rejection becomes an `Error` with `message` in the script, carrying the own properties of
 * `properties` (JSON values; `name`, `message`, and `stack` are ignored), for example `{ structuredOutput }`.
 */
export type CodemodeOutcome =
	| { ok: true; value: unknown }
	| { ok: false; message: string; properties?: Record<string, unknown> };

## CodemodeOutputItem  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/**
 * One item of the script's output, in the order the script produced it: `text()` and `console.*`
 * produce text items, with `console: true` for `console.*`, and `image()` image items. `data` is base64.
 */
export type CodemodeOutputItem =
	| { type: "text"; text: string; console?: true }
	| { type: "image"; data: string; mimeType: string };

## CodemodeResult  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/**
 * `output` is kept for failed executions too, up to the failure. `exit()` completes with `value: undefined`.
 * `during`: in a {@link CodemodeSandboxBase.start} run that the script itself ended (it returned, threw, or exited),
 * the result being processed when it did.
 */
export type CodemodeResult =
	| {
			ok: true;
			value: unknown;
			output: CodemodeOutputItem[];
			calls: CodemodeCall[];
			storeWrites: CodemodeStoreWrites;
			during?: CodemodeDuring;
	  }
	| {
			ok: false;
			error: CodemodeError;
			output: CodemodeOutputItem[];
			calls: CodemodeCall[];
			during?: CodemodeDuring;
	  };

## CodemodeRun  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** A running {@link CodemodeSandboxBase.start} execution. */
export interface CodemodeRun {
	readonly result: Promise<CodemodeResult>;
	/**
	 * Whether the run has its outcome: the script ended, timed out, or failed, or the run was aborted. Set when that is
	 * decided, before `result` settles; calls can no longer be answered. It does not mean the VM has exited.
	 */
	readonly finished: boolean;
	/**
	 * Answer call `id` as result number `seq`. Results are numbered 1, 2, ... without gaps, and the VM applies them
	 * strictly in that order, whatever order they arrive in: after a gap it waits for the missing number. While it
	 * processes this one, its clock reads `now` (ms since the epoch), or the previous value if `now` is earlier.
	 * Throws for a call that is not waiting for an answer, a `seq` used before, or a `now` that is not finite.
	 */
	deliver(seq: number, now: number, id: number, outcome: CodemodeOutcome): void;
}

## CodemodeRunOptions  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export interface CodemodeRunOptions {
	/** The VM clock's start, in ms since the epoch: `Date.now()` until the first result arrives. */
	startedAt: number;
	/** Seeds `Math.random()` and the VM's other randomness. A 32-bit unsigned integer. */
	seed: number;
	tools?: CodemodeDeclaredTool[];
	globals?: CodemodeDeclaredGlobal[];
	store?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
	signal?: AbortSignal;
	/** Deadline of this run in ms. Default: none (not the sandbox's default). */
	timeoutMs?: number;
	/** The VM's fingerprint, before the script runs and before any of its calls. */
	onStarted?(fingerprint: string): void;
	/** The script made a call. Answer it with `CodemodeRun.deliver()`, now or later. */
	onCall(call: CodemodeHostCall): void;
	/**
	 * The VM processed result `seq` (`0`: the script's first run, before any result) and waits again, having issued
	 * `issued` calls in total.
	 */
	onIdle?(seq: number, issued: number): void;
}

## CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** Options every sandbox accepts, wherever its VM runs. */
export interface CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions {
	tools?: CodemodeTool[];
	/**
	 * Functions exposed as top-level identifiers instead of on `tools`, for host helpers such as
	 * attaching an image to the result. They behave like tools (JSON round trip, promise result)
	 * but are not recorded in `result.calls`. Names must be identifiers and may not shadow the
	 * built-in globals (`tools`, `ALL_TOOLS`, `console`, `text`, `image`, `exit`, `store`, `load`).
	 */
	globals?: CodemodeTool[];
	/**
	 * Overall deadline per execution, including time spent in tools. `Infinity` disables the
	 * deadline; the execution then only ends when the script settles or is aborted.
	 * Default: 300000.
	 */
	timeoutMs?: number;
	/**
	 * Maximum memory the QuickJS VM may allocate. Allocations beyond it fail inside the script as
	 * `InternalError: out of memory`. Default: no limit beyond wasm32's 4 GiB address space.
	 */
	memoryLimitBytes?: number;
}

## CodemodeSandboxOptions  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/** Options of `CodemodeSandbox`, which runs each VM in a Node or Bun worker thread. */
export interface CodemodeSandboxOptions extends CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions {
	/**
	 * Compiled `quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm`, usually from {@link loadQuickJSWasm}. Default:
	 * `loadQuickJSWasm()`, the file in the installed `quickjs-wasi` package. Pass it when that file
	 * is not on disk, for example in a Bun compiled executable.
	 */
	wasm?: CodemodeWasmModule | Promise<CodemodeWasmModule>;
	/**
	 * Worker entry that imports `@earendil-works/pi-codemode/worker`. Default: this package's own
	 * worker file. Pass it when this package is bundled, since the default is resolved relative to
	 * the module that creates the sandbox. Bun compiled executables require the relative string
	 * specifier of an embedded build entrypoint; other hosts usually use a URL.
	 */
	workerUrl?: string | URL;
	/**
	 * Synchronously reserves capacity immediately before creating each worker, after loading wasm.
	 * Throw to deny admission without starting a worker. Return a release callback, called once if
	 * worker construction fails or when the worker actually exits, not when the result settles.
	 * The release callback must not throw. Reservations can be shared across sandbox instances.
	 */
	acquireWorker?(): () => void;
	/**
	 * Called once for each worker started by execute() or start(). `exited` resolves when that worker
	 * actually exits, which may be after the result and close() settle: on Bun a non-interruptible
	 * built-in can delay termination. Use it to keep the worker counted against host concurrency
	 * limits until it exits. A thrown callback error fails the execution and requests worker termination.
	 */
	onWorkerStarted?(exited: Promise<void>): void;
}

## CodemodeStoreWrites  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
/** Keys the script changed with `store()`. Only successful executions report writes. */
export interface CodemodeStoreWrites {
	set: Record<string, unknown>;
	/** Keys stored as `undefined`. */
	delete: string[];
}

## CodemodeTool  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export interface CodemodeTool {
	/**
	 * The script calls tools as `tools.<id>(args)`, where `<id>` is the name with characters that
	 * are not valid in identifiers replaced by `_` (see `toCodemodeIdentifier`), and also as
	 * `tools["<name>"](args)`. Globals are called as `<name>(args)` and must be identifiers, or
	 * `<namespace>.<member>`, which groups them into a frozen namespace object.
	 */
	name: string;
	/** Shown as a doc comment in {@link renderDeclarations}, and listed in `ALL_TOOLS` for tools. */
	description?: string;
	/** Schema of the single argument. Rendered as the parameter type; `unknown` when omitted. */
	inputSchema?: CodemodeJsonSchema;
	/** Schema of the resolved value. Rendered as the promise type; `unknown` when omitted. */
	outputSchema?: CodemodeJsonSchema;
	/** Globals only: `execute` receives all call arguments as an array instead of the first one. */
	spread?: boolean;
	/**
	 * Globals only: TypeScript parameter list and return type for {@link renderDeclarations}, for
	 * example `(type: string, id?: string): Promise<Model[]>`. Replaces the rendering from the schemas.
	 */
	signature?: string;
	/**
	 * `args` is whatever the script passed, after a JSON round trip. The return
	 * value must be JSON-serializable; a thrown error surfaces in the script as
	 * an `Error` with the same message.
	 */
	execute(args: unknown, context: CodemodeToolContext): Promise<unknown> | unknown;
}

## CodemodeToolContext  codemode/src/types.ts
used by: codemode-effect; durable-effect via CodemodeToolOptions
export interface CodemodeToolContext {
	/**
	 * Aborted when the script finishes (including unawaited calls), the
	 * execution times out, the caller aborts, or the sandbox is closed.
	 */
	signal: AbortSignal;
}

## CodemodeWasmModule  codemode/src/wasm.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * A compiled `WebAssembly.Module` of `quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm`. Typed opaquely because the Node
 * type definitions do not declare the WebAssembly globals (they live in the DOM lib).
 */
export type CodemodeWasmModule = object;

## loadQuickJSWasm  codemode/src/wasm.ts
used by: codemode-effect
/**
 * Read and compile the QuickJS wasm once per path. `path` defaults to the file in the installed
 * `quickjs-wasi` package; pass it when that file lives elsewhere, for example embedded in a Bun
 * compiled executable. A failed load is retried on the next call.
 */
export function loadQuickJSWasm(path?: string): Promise<CodemodeWasmModule>
